goal: Expand both master templates with explicitly authorized agent evaluation, optimization, observability, and experimental harness experience.
authorization: User explicitly requested template modification. This overrides routine immutable-template rules for these edits only; no skill, architecture, or unrelated application changes.
changes: Fintelics: functional evaluation of agent skills, prompts and tools, plus iterative comparisons before and after revisions.
RA: functional tests defined before agent runs; trajectory analysis for task adherence, out-of-scope tool calls, redundant actions, missed/extra removals; token, tool-call and runtime evaluation.

RA: separate Codex/GPT harness prototype, scoped tools, memory retrieval before edits, 12-record rolling memory and summary compaction, call limits, bounded validation retries and termination at validated submission readiness.
RA: user-confirmed unpublished experiment on 387 logging removal tasks, relative reference alignment +34%, runtime -11%, tokens approximately -20% versus native Codex/GPT.
LogRem context evaluation: use one named configuration and its own baseline, not cross-model differences or a pooled improvement.
Resume skills: agent evaluation, harness design, observability, tool calling and context engineering. CV research competencies: harness design.
rationale: Concrete implementation details and explicit metrics show agent design and evaluation experience. Keep research evaluation distinct from ERP engineering, and unpublished harness results distinct from manuscript tables.
expected_behavior: Future fresh-template applications may select these now-authorized facts. Tailor the evidence pool to each JD; do not include every bullet or carry these results into unrelated projects.

source_facts.fintelics: User describes functional testing of skills/prompts/tools and before/after efficiency and accuracy evaluation; no numeric gain supplied.
source_facts.ra_functional_evaluation: User describes TDD task construction with tests established before execution, task completion checks, trajectory/tool-call observability, and resource-use comparisons.
source_facts.custom_harness: User describes independent read/edit/log tools, memory read before code edits, the latest 12 records with summary replacement, tool-call cap, bounded validation and stop/submit when ready after successful checks.
source_facts.custom_harness_clarification: User confirmed relative 34% improvement over native Codex + GPT on 387 logging removal instances, measured by alignment with validated answers. Runtime -11% and token use about -20% supplied in original request.
source_facts.experiment_status: Custom harness experiment was not included in the paper; stated as unpublished in rendered bullets.

metric_records.interpretation: Specific observed context-setting comparison, not an overall model gain; CD expansion not supplied and not invented.

metric_records.source: Current user request and follow-up clarification
metric_records.evidence_status: User reported; raw logs and code not inspected in this task.

assumptions: The custom harness is RA research work, based on placement and user description.
No GPT version, exact validation retry limit, experiment dates or raw baseline alignment rate are inferred.
factual_checks: 34% is relative reference alignment, not 34 percentage points or generic software correctness.
Screenshot metrics stay tied to their named configuration and baseline.
TDD tests are described as assessment criteria, without claiming proof against test overfitting.
Existing dates, titles, publications and unrelated experience retained without new verification.
